sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page sapa1254 'Sapara' and subgroup page para1308 'Paravilhana-Pauxiana'
sources.note: Lists only d'Almada 1861 [1787], Koch-Grünberg 1928 and Girard 1971 (subclassification) for the language; the subgroup page cites Meira 2006, Howard 2001, Gildea 2012 for subclassification. No grammar, sketch or phonology exists for Sapará in Glottolog (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).

sources.citation: Cavalcante, Olendina de Carvalho. 2008. Memória Sapará: sociodiversidade e etnopolítica no rio Uraricoera, Roraima. Temáticas (Campinas) 16(31/32): 243-269. DOI 10.20396/tematicas.v16i31/32.12444.
sources.note: No phonology content and no Sapará words; summarises Koch-Grünberg and Migliazza 1967 on the disappearance of the language and presents oral narratives in Portuguese.

sources.citation: Meira, Sérgio. 2006. A família lingüística Caribe (Karíb). Revista de Estudos e Pesquisas (FUNAI) 3(1/2): 157-174.
sources.note: Family overview cited by Glottolog for the Paravilhana-Pauxiana subgroup; would confirm that nothing beyond wordlists exists for Sapará and may name any unpublished re-analysis of the Koch-Grünberg data.

sources.citation: Gildea, Spike. 2003. Proposing a new branch for the Cariban language family. Amerindia 28: 7-32.
sources.note: Nothing specific to Sapará. General remark on the early Cariban wordlists (which include Koch-Grünberg's Sapará list): 'I add (Gildea 1998a: 10) that most sources have been unable to reliably indicate stress. All of these flaws are found in most wordlists for most Cariban languages' — i.e. the accent marks in such lists are not to be trusted as stress data.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Sapará language' (cites Migliazza 1985, Schomburgk 1848, Gildea 2003, Kaufman 2007, Farabee 1924)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology or stress; reports Schomburgk's 1848 remark that Sapará was 'the Macusi idiom with very slight and dialectic variations'.

sources.citation: Durbin, Marshall. 1977. A survey of the Carib language family. In Ellen B. Basso (ed.), Carib-Speaking Indians: Culture, Society and Language (Anthropological Papers of the University of Arizona 28), 23-38. Tucson: University of Arizona Press. (Open-access Manifold edition, University of Arizona Press.)
sources.note: No phonology of Sapará. Sapara appears three times, in lists: 'Theodor Koch-Grünberg, who compiled vocabularies of no less than 10 Carib languages.. Ingariko, and Sapara (1928). Although Koch-Grünberg attempted little classification, his phonetic details are so excellent that they have contributed a great deal toward our understanding of the groupings of Carib languages'; de Goeje's second volume 'gives information on some additional languages.. Sapara, Sikiyana..'; and the East-West Guiana Carib membership list. The words stress/accent/tone do not occur in the chapter.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Cestmir. 1968. Classification of South American Indian languages (ed. Johannes Wilbert). Los Angeles: Latin American Center, UCLA. 453 pp.
sources.note: 'Zapara or Sapara - spoken in the middle and eastern parts of Maraca Island. [Koch-Grunberg 1913, p. 455, 1928, pp. 258-272.]' Entry only; nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: Migliazza, Ernesto. 1967. Grupos lingüísticos do Território Federal de Roraima. In Herman Lent (ed.), Atas do Simpósio sôbre a Biota Amazônica, vol. 2 (Antropologia), 153-173. Rio de Janeiro: Conselho Nacional de Pesquisas.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No Sapará language data. The survey reports only that 'Integrados com os Makuxi nas malocas Mangueira e Aningal.. foram encontrados cinco indivíduos que dizem ser descendentes dos Sapará (dois) e Wayumará (três), tribos Karib que antigamente habitavam a região.' Phoneme charts are given for Makuxi and other living languages only.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1928. Vom Roroima zum Orinoco. Ergebnisse einer Reise in Nordbrasilien und Venezuela in den Jahren 1911-1913. Vierter Band: Sprachen. Stuttgart: Strecker und Schröder. Section 'Sapará, Purukotó, Wayumará', pp. 257-272; 'Zur Transskription', pp. 2-3.
sources.note: The only primary linguistic data on Sapará: a three-column comparative wordlist (Sapará / Purukotó / Wayumará) with acute accent marks on the forms (p. 258: onú 'Zunge', uyóe 'Zahn', uyonaí 'Nase', uyonayatáń 'Nasenloch', uyo:nú 'Auge', upa:naí 'Ohr', apepé, une:kapú 'Kopf', ipo:putú 'Kopfhaar', uyomekúń 'Arm'; p. 257 eleuta-ké 'setze dich!', iue:-ké 'töte!', mia:lé 'vorwärts!'), i.e. the accent mostly sits on the final syllable of citation forms; but no stress rule is stated anywhere. The general 'Zur Transskription' note (pp. 2-3) only says that i/u bearing an accent count as diphthong memb…

sources.citation: Farabee, William Curtis. 1924. The Central Caribs. University Museum Anthropological Publications 10. Philadelphia. 'Zaparas', pp. 242-243.
sources.note: Ethnographic note only: three full-bloods remained c. 1914, the mother 'speaks only her own language, which is very closely related to Macusi'; a vocabulary is given for Azumara but none for Zapara; nothing on accent.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1923. Vom Roroima zum Orinoco. Bd. 3: Ethnographie. Stuttgart: Strecker und Schröder. Section 'Sapará, Wayumará, Purukotó', pp. 6-8.
sources.note: Ethnographic and historical only ('Von ihren Sprachen konnte ich noch in letzter Stunde Material sammeln. Als Stammesgemeinschaften haben sie aufgehört zu bestehen'); no phonology content.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1917. Vom Roroima zum Orinoco: Ergebnisse einer Reise in Nordbrasilien und Venezuela in den Jahren 1911-1913. Bd. 1: Schilderung der Reise. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer.
sources.note: Documents the circumstances of the only Sapará record: 'beendige ich die Sprachaufnahme des Sapará mit einem älteren Manne dieses Stammes.. Es ist ein bisher unbekannter Karaibendialekt, den ich in den wichtigsten Vergleichswörtern festgelegt habe, sehr verschieden vom Makuschi und seinen Verwandten.' No remark on accent, stress or tone.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1913. Abschluss meiner Reise durch Nordbrasilien zum Orinoco, mit besonderer Berücksichtigung der von mir besuchten Indianerstämme. Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 45: 448-474.
sources.note: Cited in the 1928 volume (p. 257) for the Purukotó/Sapará situation; ethnographic report from the same trip, unlikely but possible to carry a remark on the sound of the language.

sources.citation: d'Almada, Manuel da Gama Lobo. 1861 [1787]. Descripção relativa ao Rio Branco e seu território. Revista Trimensal do Instituto Historico, Geographico e Ethnographico do Brasil 24: 617-683.
sources.note: Only an ethnographic paragraph 'Saparás' (pp. 678-679: they live on the Mucajaí, deserted the Portuguese settlements, led the 1781 killings); no vocabulary and nothing about the language found in the scanned.

sources.citation: Schomburgk, Robert H. 1849. Remarks to accompany a Comparative Vocabulary of eighteen Languages and Dialects of Indian Tribes inhabiting Guiana. In: Report of the Eighteenth Meeting of the British Association for the Advancement of Science, held at Swansea in August 1848. Notices and Abstracts of Communications (Transactions of the Sections, Ethnology), pp. 96-99. London: John Murray.
sources.note: Nothing on Zapara (Sapará) accent or tone in the readable text. The notice gives the provisional six-section division ('I. Caribi-Tamanakan.—1., Caribisi. 2. Accawai. § Waika. 3. Macusi. § Zapara. 4. Arecuna. § Soerikong. 5. Waiyamara..'), says the comparative vocabulary 'consists merely of eighteen words' per language, and closes with remarks on North American affinities. The table itself (pp. 97-98) and its 'Remarks.—Orthography adopted in the above vocabularies' footnote (vowels as in Italian, g hard, etc.) are printed sideways and come out rotated/garbled in the scanned, so whether the Za…

sources.citation: Gildea, Spike. 2012. Linguistic studies in the Cariban family. In Lyle Campbell & Verónica Grondona (eds.), The Indigenous Languages of South America: A Comprehensive Guide, 441-494. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.note: Standard survey of Cariban documentation; lists Sapará as extinct with wordlist-only documentation; would settle whether any later descriptive work exists.

sources.citation: Girard, Victor. 1971. Proto-Carib phonology. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley. ii+363 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only linguistic work Glottolog lists for Sapará; a comparative reconstruction that re-uses Koch-Grünberg's Sapará forms and may comment on the accent notation of the 1928 wordlists — the closest thing to an analysis of Sapará stress that could exist.

sources.citation: Cavalcante, Olendina de Carvalho. 2010. A política da memória Sapará. Tese de doutorado (Antropologia Social), Universidade Estadual de Campinas. Orientadora: Nádia Farage.
